title: A bigger black sweater
goal: Make adjectives agree with their nouns, and learn one rule that trips up English speakers but is easy once you see it: in a word group, only the **first** word may carry the article.
bekal: making adjectives agree with the gender and number of the noun
putting the definite article on adjectives
using the demonstratives **този / тази / това / тези**
shopping for clothes from start to finish

dialogs.title: Диалог — At the clothes shop
dialogs.intro: Ani is looking for a sweater for her first winter. Watch how the adjective ending changes every time the item being talked about changes.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: I'm looking for a black sweater.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Medium. What do you think of this one?

lines.speaker: Продавачка:
lines.id: The black one is nice, but the gray one is warmer.
lines.literal: black-the — is — nice, but — gray-the — is — warmer.

lines.speaker: Продавачка:
lines.id: Of course. The fitting room is over there.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: It's a bit tight. Do you have a bigger one?

lines.speaker: Продавачка:
lines.id: Here's the large size. It looks great on you.
lines.literal: here-is — large-the — size. stands — to-you — very — well.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: I'll take it. How much is it?

lines.speaker: Продавачка:
lines.id: Forty-five leva. At the register, please.
lines.literal: forty — and — five — leva. at — register-the, please.

notes: **Bulgarian adjectives have four forms, and three of them just add one letter.** The masculine is the base form; the feminine adds **-а**, the neuter adds **-о**, the plural adds **-и**. *Хубав, хубава, хубаво, хубави.* Learn one form and you practically know all four.

⚠️ **Many masculine adjectives slip in an е or ъ that disappears again in the other forms.** *Черен* (black) → *черна, черно, черни*. *Топъл* (warm) → *топла, топло, топли*. *Тесен* (tight) → *тясна…* That extra letter in the masculine is called a fleeting vowel, and it only lives there. Learn adjectives by their **feminine** form if you want a cleaner pattern.

⚠️ **Голям changes even more: голям → голяма → голямо → големи.** The **я** turns into **е** in the plural. This я/е switch happens in a group of Bulgarian words, and the rule is: **я** is used when the next syllable has no *е* or *и*. You don't need to work it out — just memorize the pairs *голям / големи*, *бял / бели* (white), *цял / цели* (whole).

**Черният е хубав — an adjective can stand alone without its noun.** Once the item is clear from the conversation, the noun can be dropped and the article sits on the adjective. English does the same with "one": "the black one is nice".
**Може ли да го пробвам — the short pronoun го stands in for the sweater.** *Пуловер* is masculine, so *го*. If you were trying on a *риза* (shirt, feminine), the sentence would be *да я пробвам*.
**Стои ви добре literally means "stands to you well"** and means "it suits you, it looks good on you". Same pattern for shoes, glasses, colors. If it doesn't suit you: *Не ми стои добре.*

**Какъв размер носите? — the question word какъв also follows gender**: *какъв* (masc.), *каква* (fem.), *какво* (neut.), *какви* (pl.). Note that *какво* meaning "what" is the same word as the neuter form. *Каква е тя?* — what is she like?
**Взимам го — "I'll take it" — is the line that closes the deal.** It works exactly like "I'll take it" in English. The seller will point you straight to the *касата* (register).

grammars.title: Adjectives follow their noun
body: Four forms, chosen by the noun that follows. The adjective always stands **before** its noun.
after: *Хубав град* (a nice city), *хубава книга* (a nice book), *хубаво дете* (a nice child), *хубави книги* (nice books). The plural is the same for all three genders — one form for everything.

grammars.title: The definite article on adjectives — and one iron rule
body: When there is an adjective, the definite article moves onto it. The noun is left bare.
after: ⚠️ **One word group, one article, and it sits on the first word.** Never *черният пуловерът*. With two adjectives, the article still goes only on the first: *големият черен пуловер* (the big black sweater).
Note that masculine adjectives use **-ият / -ия**, following the same long/short rule as masculine nouns in Unit 3: the long form for the subject, the short form everywhere else.

grammars.title: Demonstratives: this and that
body: Four forms for "this", four for "that". Both follow the gender of the noun, and the noun after them takes **no** article.
after: In everyday speech, *онзи* is rarely used; people just say *този* while pointing, or add *там* (there). And **това** on its own means "this" in general: *Какво е това?* (What is this?), *Това е моят пуловер.*

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Син (blue) is irregular**: *син, синя, синьо, сини*. It is the only color whose neuter uses **ьо**, one of the few places the letter **ь** shows up in Bulgarian.

sections.title: Shopping for clothes from start to finish

blocks.text: The last line is the politest way to leave a shop without buying. **Ще помисля** — "I'll think about it" — is understood everywhere as a gentle no, just as in English. Nobody is offended.

blocks.title: Red and white, the colors that keep coming back
items: If you look closely at Bulgarian things, two colors keep appearing together: red and white. They are on the March *мартеница*, on the embroidery of traditional clothes, on the woven carpets of Чипровци.
Red stands for blood, life and the sun; white for purity and long life. The pairing is far older than the modern state, and Bulgarians will be glad if you ask about it.
A sentence to get the story going: *Защо мартеницата е червена и бяла?* (Why is the martenitsa red and white?)

exercises.prompt: Make the adjective agree with the noun.
Put the definite article on the adjective. For masculine, write the LONG form.
Put the words in the right order.
Fill in този, тази, това or тези.

answers: черен — черна — ново — нови — голяма — големи
черният пуловер — хубавата книга — голямото дете — старите обувки — новият град
Търся черен пуловер. — Може ли да го пробвам? — Стои ми добре. — Имате ли по-голям? — Взимам го.
